title: Every Chief Minister Showed Up to NITI Aayog for the First Time. Modi Wants GDP Data Down to the District.
excerpt: The 11th Governing Council meeting ended a years-long streak of opposition boycotts and put district-level economic measurement at the centre of India's 2047 development push.
body:
For the first time since NITI Aayog replaced the Planning Commission in 2015, all 28 chief ministers sat in the same room. No walkouts. No boycotts. No empty chairs where Tamil Nadu or West Bengal or Kerala used to leave a political point.

The 11th Governing Council meeting, held at Rashtrapati Bhavan Cultural Centre on Thursday, broke a pattern that had defined the body's annual gatherings. In 2023, nine chief ministers stayed away. The year before, four opposition leaders — including West Bengal's Mamata Banerjee and Bihar's then-chief minister Nitish Kumar — refused to attend. This time, newly installed leaders including C. Joseph Vijay from Tamil Nadu, Suvendu Adhikari from West Bengal, D.K. Shivakumar from Karnataka, and V.D. Satheesan from Kerala all made the trip to Delhi.

The shift is partly arithmetic — several states changed governments in recent elections — but it also reflects a pragmatic calculation. With India navigating the economic fallout of the Iran conflict, rising fuel costs and a global trade environment being reshaped by tariffs, even opposition chief ministers appear to have concluded that sitting outside the room carries a higher cost than sitting inside it.

## District-Level GDP: The Centrepiece

Prime Minister Narendra Modi used the meeting to push an idea that could reshape how India measures — and funds — development. He urged states to develop district-level GDP estimates, arguing that national and state-level numbers mask enormous variation within states.

The logic is straightforward: India's growth story is concentrated in a handful of urban corridors. District-level data would expose which areas are being left behind, force accountability on local administrators and give the Centre a granular map to target investment. NITI Aayog Vice Chairperson Ashok Kumar Lahiri confirmed that the council discussed creating structured mechanisms to track short, medium and long-term outcomes at the district level.

For NRIs considering investments back home, district-level GDP data would be a game-changer. Currently, choosing between setting up a facility in, say, Coimbatore versus Madurai involves patchy data and anecdotal evidence. Standardised district-level numbers would bring transparency to those decisions.

## Energy Anxiety Dominated the Room

Several chief ministers used the platform to flag rising energy costs — a direct consequence of the Iran crisis that has pushed Brent crude above $90 a barrel for months. Discussions focused on expanding rooftop solar installations for homes, schools, hospitals and government buildings to reduce dependence on grid electricity and manage subsidy burdens that are straining state budgets.

The energy conversation is especially pointed for manufacturing-heavy states competing for the foreign investment that India's trade agreements are meant to attract. Competitive energy pricing was identified as a prerequisite for states to absorb the industrial capacity that firms are looking to relocate from China.

## Women, Youth and Defence Manufacturing

Modi called on states to double the number of 'Lakhpati Didis' — women who earn at least one lakh rupees annually through self-help groups — from 3 crore to 6 crore. He also highlighted India's demographic profile, noting that nearly 70 crore Indians are under 25, and urged states to convert this into a 'development dividend' through education and skilling.

The Prime Minister pushed states to explore opportunities in defence manufacturing, saying India is establishing a distinct identity in the sector, and to attract investments from countries with which India has signed trade agreements. He specifically asked states to strengthen One District One Product initiatives and build export-oriented strategies around them.

## The AFSPA Signal

In a notable announcement at the margins of the meeting, Home Minister Amit Shah said the government plans to remove the Armed Forces Special Powers Act from the entire Northeast except one or two states by next year. The statement signals a significant confidence in the security situation across the region and could open new economic corridors in states that have long been treated as security zones rather than investment destinations.

## What It Means

Full attendance at NITI Aayog does not mean full agreement. Opposition chief ministers used the platform to press their own demands — affordable energy, greater fiscal autonomy, and more equitable resource allocation. But the fact that they chose to press those demands inside the room rather than from outside it represents a shift in India's federal dynamics that could outlast any single meeting.

The real test will be whether district-level GDP estimates materialise. India has announced ambitious data projects before. The difference this time is that every state government has, at minimum, signalled buy-in.
